complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Add Authentication Support for Inbox Endpoints and HTTP Destinations
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down authentication implementation into: 1) Define InboxAuthConfig and DestinationAuthConfig sealed classes in QueueBoxConfig.kt with Bearer, ApiKey, HMAC-SHA256 variants for inbox and OAuth2, Basic, Header variants for destinations. 2) Create InboxAuthValidator class in inbox-service with constant-time comparison and HMAC signature computation. 3) Create OAuth2TokenManager with token caching, mutex-based refresh, and concurrent-safe access in outbox-service. 4) Create DestinationAuthResolver to map auth configs to HTTP headers. 5) Update InboxRoutes.kt to integrate DoubleReceive plugin and auth validation before handler. 6) Update HttpPublisher to inject auth resolver and merge auth headers. 7) Add validation rules to ConfigValidator for auth configurations and update SourceConfig.Http and DestinationConfig.Http to include auth fields.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task is highly complex due to multiple auth mechanisms (Bearer, API Key, HMAC-SHA256 for inbox; OAuth2, Basic, Header for destinations). It requires: (1) Adding new sealed class hierarchies to QueueBoxConfig.kt, (2) Creating new auth package with InboxAuthValidator requiring secure HMAC computation and constant-time comparison, (3) Creating OAuth2TokenManager with concurrent token caching and mutex-based refresh, (4) Modifying InboxRoutes.kt to buffer request body for HMAC validation using DoubleReceive plugin, (5) Updating HttpPublisher to merge auth headers, (6) Adding ConfigValidator rules for all auth variants, (7) Extensive testing for security-critical code. The security-sensitive nature and cross-cutting concerns (inbox-service, outbox-service, config, core) increase complexity. The OAuth2 token manager alone requires careful concurrent access handling.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Add Custom Column Name Mapping for Inbox and Outbox Tables
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down column mapping implementation into: 1) Define ColumnMappingConfig, OutboxColumnMapping, and InboxColumnMapping data classes in QueueBoxConfig.kt with defaults matching existing schema. 2) Create DynamicTables.kt in postgres module with DynamicOutboxTable and DynamicInboxTable classes that accept column mapping. 3) Update InboxRepository and OutboxRepository to accept column mapping, update all raw SQL strings to use mapped column names including CTE queries. 4) Create SqlServerDynamicTables.kt and update SqlServerInboxRepository and SqlServerOutboxRepository similarly with proper reserved word escaping. 5) Update PostgresRepositoryFactory and SqlServerRepositoryFactory to pass column mapping from config. 6) Add SQL identifier validation to ConfigValidator ensuring column names are safe from injection.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task has significant complexity because it requires modifying raw SQL queries across 4 repository files (InboxRepository.kt, OutboxRepository.kt, SqlServerInboxRepository.kt, SqlServerOutboxRepository.kt). The repositories use complex CTEs (lines 48-79 in InboxRepository, 76-107 in SqlServerInboxRepository) that have hardcoded column names throughout. Each column reference must be replaced with mapped values. Additionally: (1) Need dynamic table definitions instead of static object declarations, (2) SQL Server requires bracket escaping for reserved words like 'key', (3) ResultSet.toInboxMessage/toOutboxMessage methods (lines 136-150 in InboxRepository, 164-174 in SqlServerInboxRepository) use hardcoded column names in getString() calls, (4) SQL injection prevention requires careful identifier validation. The task touches both PostgreSQL and SQL Server implementations with their different syntaxes.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Add Dynamic Payload-Based RabbitMQ Routing Key Templates
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down routing key template enhancement into: 1) Create RoutingKeyRenderer class in outbox-service that parses mustache-style placeholders and extracts payload fields using JSON path traversal, supporting {{ topic }}, {{ payload.field }}, and {{ data.nested.field }} patterns. 2) Update MessageRouter.route() to accept optional payload parameter and use RoutingKeyRenderer instead of simple string replacement, keeping backward compatibility. 3) Update OutboxPoller.processMessage() to pass message.payload to router.route() call. 4) Add routingKeyMissingFieldDefault optional field to RouteConfig and add comprehensive tests for template rendering including nested fields and missing field defaults.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task is moderately complex but well-scoped. The existing MessageRouter.renderTemplate (lines 61-66) only does simple {{ topic }} replacement. The enhancement requires: (1) Creating RoutingKeyRenderer with regex-based placeholder parsing and JSON path traversal for nested fields, (2) Updating route() method signature to optionally accept payload (line 36), (3) Updating OutboxPoller.processMessage (line 56) to pass payload. The TransformEngine already demonstrates JSON field extraction patterns that can be referenced. RabbitPublisher also has template rendering (lines 34-36) but uses the Destination.RabbitMQ.routingKeyTemplate which is separate from route-level templates. The change is additive and backward-compatible since payload is optional. Testing is straightforward with unit tests for template rendering.
